info.title: ownsi API
info.description:
Prove ownership of a domain with a TXT record, and read a zone before anyone signs in.

Two surfaces, and they behave differently on purpose:

- `GET /api/zones/:name` is public. It streams what DNS answers, in the order DNS answers it,
  and writes nothing. No account, no key.
- Everything under `/api/domains`, `/api/claims` and `/api/verifications` belongs to an
  account and needs a session cookie.

A lookup that failed never carries records, and a claim that has not been checked never carries a
diagnosis: both are tagged unions, so the shape tells you which case you are in. Errors are always
`{ error: { code, message, docsUrl } }` with a stable `code`.

servers.description: The origin the front end and the API share

tags.name: Zones
tags.description: Reading a zone the way a visitor sees it: the delegation first, so the provider can be named, then how long publishing is likely to take. Public, rate limited per IP.

tags.name: Domains
tags.description: A name on an account, and nothing else — no status, no token. It is what a claim is opened against. Session required.

tags.name: Claims
tags.description: The episode: one token, one seven-day window, one outcome. A claim is never reopened, so the list of them is the account's history. Session required.

tags.name: Events
tags.description: One stream per open tab, telling an account's screens what moved. It carries no state: a message names the resource, the client reads it back. Session required.

tags.name: Proof
tags.description: A proved claim, shared. A link carries its own slug — never the DNS token — and resolves for seven days at `/p/:slug`, where the page states one moment and reads no DNS. Session required to publish one.

tags.name: Verifications
tags.description: The process behind a claim: the runs it has made, the named diagnosis of the last one, and when the next lands. Session required.

get.description: Server-sent events, one connection per open tab. Every message arrives on the default `message` event and its `type` field says what moved; it carries no state of its own, so the client reads the resource back over its own route. A `heartbeat` every twenty seconds keeps the connection off an idle proxy's timer and tells a client that has heard nothing that it is still connected.

200.description: The stream, open until the client closes it.

get.description: Streams the reading in the order DNS answers it: the delegation first, so the provider can be named, then the publishing estimate. No account needed; nothing is written to DNS.

post.summary: Put a domain on this account
post.description: Idempotent on the name: asking twice returns the same domain. It carries no status of its own — open a claim to start proving it.

get.summary: List the domains on this account
get.description: Newest first, one page at a time: pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next one. Each domain carries the state of the claim in play on it, and `counts` tallies every status on the account, not only this page. `name` narrows to one, which is how a page reads a domain it only knows by name. Archived domains are left out; they are still readable by id.
The name and when it joined the account. Its claims are their own resource.

delete.summary: Erase this domain and everything it carried
delete.description: The only eraser. Its claims, their notices and their verifications go with it, and any proof link stops resolving. Archiving is what you want if you only wanted it off the list.

post.summary: Stop involving me with this name
post.description: Leaves the list and ends any open claim on it. Nothing is retracted: a proof keeps its dates and its links resolve.

post.summary: Open a claim on a domain
post.description: Mints the token, opens the seven-day window and starts the verification that runs against it. The record to create comes back with the claim; the process comes back as `verificationId`.

get.summary: List the claims on this account
get.description: Newest first, every state included — a claim is never deleted, so the list is the account's history. Narrow it to one domain with `domainId`.
The token, the record to create, the window it runs in — and whether another account has proved the same name, which takes nothing away from this one.

post.description: The token stops being accepted from here on and the verification stops running. Claiming the domain again issues a new one.

post.summary: Publish a link to this proof
post.description: Idempotent while one is live: asking twice hands back the same slug. The slug is its own — never the DNS token — and it stops resolving after seven days.

get.summary: List the links published for this proof
get.description: Newest first, expired and revoked ones included — what was shared is part of the record. `standing` says which of them still resolves.

post.description: The slug stops resolving from here on. It retracts nothing: the proof keeps its date, and any other link to it keeps working.

get.description: Where the process is: the named diagnosis of the last run, when the next one lands, and the deadline it is running against.

get.summary: List the attempts behind a verification
get.description: Every read this verification has made, newest first — the evidence a proof rests on, and the record of the failures that came before it.

post.description: Reads DNS now instead of waiting for the next scheduled run, and answers with what the read found: the proof, or the named reason the record is not there.
